title: Summary writing
examples: How do I know what is important enough to include in my summary?
Is it okay to use my own words even if I know the exact phrase?
What is the difference between summarizing and just shortening the text?

explain.say: Today we are learning how to write a good summary.
First, you must select the most important ideas from the text.
Next, you need to paraphrase those selected ideas in your own words.
Then, you must write with concision, meaning you use few words.
For an everyday example, imagine you read a recipe for bread.
A common mistake is copying too many phrases from the original text.

faq.q: How long should my summary be?
faq.a: A good rule is to aim for about one-quarter the length of the original text. You are aiming for a shorter version.
asks: What is a good length for a summary?

faq.q: Do I need to include my opinion in the summary?
faq.a: No, a summary must only report what the original author said. It should be objective and neutral.
asks: Can I add what I think about it?

faq.q: What if the text has many different topics?
faq.a: You should group related ideas together to show the main themes. Think about the main message connecting them all.
asks: How do I handle multiple topics?

faq.q: Is it better to use bullet points or full sentences?
faq.a: Unless the instructions say otherwise, full, flowing sentences are usually best for a formal summary. This helps show good writing flow.
asks: Should I use lists or paragraphs?

faq.q: What is the difference between summarizing and retelling?
faq.a: Retelling includes details and sometimes your own interpretation. Summarizing focuses only on the core, main points.
asks: Is summarizing the same as retelling?

facts: A summary captures the main idea of a text.
Paraphrasing means restating someone else's words in your own words.
Concision means using the fewest words possible without losing meaning.
A summary should remain neutral and objective.

quiz.say: The main message of the passage was that the species declined because its home and environment were damaged.
quiz.show: The main idea was habitat damage.

options.show: The species declined due to changes in its diet.
options.say: The species declined due to changes in its diet.

options.show: The species declined because it was too cold.
options.say: The species declined because it was too cold.

options.show: The species declined because its home and environment were damaged.
options.say: The species declined because its home and environment were damaged.

options.show: Habitat loss and pollution caused the species to decline.
options.say: Habitat loss and pollution caused the species to decline.

quiz.why: This correctly identifies the core cause mentioned in the text, which is the main point.

wrong.0: This introduces information not mentioned in the passage.
wrong.1: This focuses on only one factor, ignoring the broader environmental damage.
wrong.3: This is too specific because it only names two causes, missing others.

quiz.say: To paraphrase a sentence, you should:
quiz.show: Paraphrase: Change the words, keep the meaning.

options.show: Write it in a question format.
options.say: Write it in a question format.

options.show: Use different vocabulary and sentence structure.
options.say: Use different vocabulary and sentence structure.

quiz.why: This shows you are changing the wording while keeping the original meaning intact.

wrong.0: Changing only a few words is not enough; you need to restructure the whole idea.
wrong.1: The summary should state facts, not ask questions.
wrong.2: The language should remain appropriate for the original text's tone.

quiz.say: If a text is very wordy, what should you do to make it concise?

options.show: Replace every noun with a verb.
options.say: Replace every noun with a verb.

options.show: Add more examples to make it clearer.
options.say: Add more examples to make it clearer.

quiz.why: Removing extra descriptive words helps keep the sentence direct and focused on the facts.

wrong.0: This will change the meaning of the sentence entirely.
wrong.1: Adding more detail defeats the purpose of being concise.
wrong.2: Complex words do not equal conciseness; simple, direct words are better.
